input.command: ls -R src; cat -n src/store.ts; cat -n src/routes.ts
input.description: List source files and show store and routes

input.command: grep -rn "system" --include=* . 2>/dev/null | grep -v node_modules | grep -v "^./.git/" | head -30; ls -a; cat -n src/git-auth.ts | head -40
input.description: Search for system owner references and docs
Check route wiring and admin checks

input.reason: In src/store.ts, Store.deleteRepo sends admins down an unrestricted DELETE (line 26). For everyone else it runs `DELETE FROM repos WHERE id = ? AND (owner = ? OR owner = 'system')` (line 29). The `OR owner = 'system'` clause means a non-admin's delete matches both their own rows and every row owned by 'system'. The route handler in src/routes.ts, deleteRepo (lines 26-33), does no check of its own. It passes req.params.id and req.user straight to store.deleteRepo, and the only guard left is the SQL filter. Nothing else in the repository limits this: there is no role check, no middleware in routes.ts, no test, and no comment saying non-admins should be able to delete system repos. The admin/non-admin split shows the non-admin branch is meant to be owner-scoped, and the extra clause breaks that. Both findings describe the same defect: F13 covers the route that reaches it and F16 covers the filter.
input.failure_scenario: A shared repository row exists with owner 'system'. An authenticated user with oid 'u123' and isAdmin=false calls the deleteRepo route with that repo's id. src/routes.ts:28 calls store.deleteRepo(id, {oid:'u123', isAdmin:false}). The SQL at src/store.ts:29 matches because owner = 'system', so the row is deleted, changes is 1, and the route returns 204. The shared repository is now gone for every user.
input.severity_reason: This is a broken authorization check that lets any authenticated user permanently delete shared system repositories, which is data loss. I rated it High rather than Critical because nothing in this repository creates rows owned by 'system': registerRepo always sets owner to req.user.oid. So the impact depends on system rows being seeded somewhere outside this code.
